chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar has been transmitted by me from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with them both), from Sa'd ibn Abdullah and Al-Himyari together, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr together, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar Al-Dahni Al-Ghanawi Al-Kufi, the freed servant of Bujaylah, and he was known by the kunya Abu Al-Qasim.

key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ: Abu Al-Qasim, the kunya (father of the name) of Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar.
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: May Allah be pleased with them both, a phrase of respect used for the two Imams.
key_terms.مَوْلَى: Freed servant or client, indicating a social relationship of patronage.
key_terms.مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, a prominent companion of the Imams and a key narrator.
key_terms.يُكَنَّى: He was known by his kunya (teknonym).

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar in this hadith collection?
ai.summary: This passage highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous methodology in verifying the isnad for Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, a key Kufi narrator often cited in Shia jurisprudence. By tracing the chain through prominent figures like al-Saffar and al-Humayri, the text underscores the scholarly rigor applied to establishing the authenticity of reports from this specific transmitter.
